key_insight: A multimodal graph neural network can accurately prioritize cancer immunotherapy targets by integrating molecular, spatial and clinical data, and top predictions were functionally validated using patient-derived tumour explants.
problem_solved: Addresses the gap between computational target prediction and clinically relevant validation, enabling more reliable identification of actionable immunotherapy targets from heterogeneous biomedical data.
method: Constructed a multimodal graph neural network that fuses molecular profiles, gene/protein interaction networks, spatial/tumour microenvironment features and clinical annotations.
Trained to distinguish approved and prospective immunotherapy targets and benchmarked against standard classifiers.
Functionally validated high-confidence predictions using a clinically relevant patient-derived tumour explant (PDE) platform.
impact: Shows how GNNs can integrate heterogeneous biomedical modalities for translational discovery and underscores the importance of experimental validation—guiding AI practitioners toward clinically actionable ML workflows.
visual_elements: Schematic of the multimodal GNN architecture showing inputs (molecular, spatial, interaction, clinical) converging into node-level target scores.
Performance chart (ROC/PR) comparing the GNN to baseline models and highlighting recovery of approved targets.
Network diagram highlighting top predicted targets and their connections to immune pathways.
Flow diagram or photo-illustration of the patient-derived tumour explant validation pipeline linking prediction → ex vivo assay → functional readout.
paper_title: Immunotherapy drug target identification using machine learning and patient-derived tumour explant validation
paper_authors: Marcellus Augustine, Nuno Rocha Nene, Hongchang Fu, Christopher L. Pinder, Lorena Ligammari
